summary: Thoroughly tested the new PAPER<->LIVE trading mode toggle (safety-critical feature). All backend behaviors (GO LIVE confirm gating, case-sensitive exact match, auto-trader block in live mode, real account-number switch between paper/live Alpaca accounts, no-confirm-needed switch back to paper, and restart persistence with startup auto-trader force-off safety net) verified correct via a new pytest file. Frontend flow (Settings toggle, GO LIVE modal with disabled/enabled confirm button, red persistent banner app-wide, nav badge, Scanner auto-trade-toggle block with toast) verified end-to-end via Playwright and confirmed matching backend state. Environment left in PAPER mode with auto-trader inactive at the end, as required.

minor.issue: test_security_and_trading.py::TestAutoTrader::test_manual_process_trigger_no_arity_bug is a pre-existing flaky 502 under live-data load (already documented in iteration_14.json, not related to this feature). test_auth_and_account_safety.py::TestBruteForceLockout also showed intermittent flakiness in one full-suite run - likely lockout state timing sensitivity, not something introduced by this feature.

action_items: No action items - feature works correctly end to end.

Optional: consider isolating test_security_and_trading.py's auto-trader toggle test so it doesn't leave auto_trader.active=True as global mutable state that can race with other stateful tests when run in parallel (pytest-xdist -n2); not urgent, cosmetic to test suite only.
critical_code_review_comments: alpaca_service.py correctly maintains two fully separate TradingClient instances (paper always paper=True, live always paper=False) and only instantiates the live client if ALPACA_DATA_API_KEY genuinely differs from ALPACA_API_KEY - verified live_available=true and account_number differs between modes (confirmed real account switch, not cosmetic).
server.py's /trading-mode POST correctly requires exact-match 'GO LIVE' (case-sensitive) only when switching TO live, and allows switching back to paper unconditionally - matches spec exactly.

Defense-in-depth for auto-trader is solid: blocked at toggle endpoint (400), forced off when switching to live via POST /trading-mode, forced off again in auto_trader_loop() as an extra guard, and forced off again on server startup if the persisted mode restores to live with a stale active=true flag. Verified via restart test that this safety net works.
Trading mode persistence via db.app_config._id='trading_mode' correctly survives a supervisor restart, and restoration properly does NOT re-enable auto-trader.

Minor test-infra note (already fixed by me): my new test module is inherently stateful/order-dependent since it mutates a single shared backend's trading_mode flag; I added pytest.mark.xdist_group to pin it to one worker (pytest.ini's loadscope only pins per-class, and this module has multiple classes) and gated the destructive supervisor-restart test behind RUN_RESTART_TEST=1 so it doesn't disrupt other concurrently-running tests in default full-suite runs. Restart test was independently verified passing when run with RUN_RESTART_TEST=1 -n 0.

context_for_next_testing_agent: New file /app/backend/tests/test_trading_mode_toggle.py covers the paper/live toggle end to end. It uses pytest.mark.xdist_group(name='trading_mode_toggle') to force sequential execution of its classes under the default -n 2 --dist loadscope config (necessary since this feature has shared mutable state across the whole module, not just within one class). Its restart-persistence test is skipped by default (guarded by RUN_RESTART_TEST=1 env var) since it performs an actual `supervisorctl restart backend` which would otherwise kill in-flight requests for other tests running concurrently in the default full-suite run; run it explicitly with `RUN_RESTART_TEST=1 python -m pytest tests/test_trading_mode_toggle.py -n 0` when specifically verifying restart persistence. Environment confirmed left in PAPER mode with auto_trader.active=false at the end of this session.
rca of the issue: No product bugs found. One self-inflicted test-infra issue during this session: initially wrote the new trading-mode test module without any worker-pinning, and pytest.ini's default `-n 2 --dist loadscope` distributed different classes of the same stateful module across both workers, causing race conditions (one worker's GO-LIVE test running concurrently with another's should-still-be-paper assertion). Root cause: loadscope groups tests by class scope, not module scope, so a multi-class module sharing global backend state needs an explicit xdist_group marker to guarantee sequential execution. Fixed by adding pytestmark = pytest.mark.xdist_group(name='trading_mode_toggle') and by gating the disruptive live supervisor-restart sub-test behind an explicit opt-in env var.
